title: agno-agi/agno v3.1.9 — v3.1.9
body:
# Changelog

## New Features:

- **MCP Tool Runner**: `POST /mcp/server/tools/{tool_name}/run` runs any tool listed on the AgentOS Server Card over HTTP and returns its result, so a tool can be tested without an MCP client. Turn it off with `MCPConfig(tool_run_endpoint=False)`. See [cookbook](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/main/cookbook/05_agent_os/14_mcp/inspect_tools.py).

## Bug Fixes:

- **AgentOS MCP Server**: `/mcp` and `/mcp/server-card` now accept browser requests from origins the AgentOS CORS policy allows, so `os.agno.com` can reach the MCP server of a local AgentOS. `/info` now reports the configured MCP path instead of always `/mcp`.
- **Postgres Metrics**: Metrics refresh on a migrated database no longer loads the legacy `sessions.runs` column into memory.
- **Function Workflows**: A function passed as a workflow's `steps` now runs once when its body raises a `TypeError`, and sync functions and generators now work with `arun()`.
- **AgenticChunking**: Chunking no longer hangs when the model returns a zero or negative breakpoint, and `max_chunk_size` must be greater than `0`.
- **BaiduSearchTools**: Chinese titles and abstracts are returned as readable text instead of `\uXXXX` escapes.
- **Human-in-the-Loop User Input**: A `requires_user_input` tool with a parameter typed `int | None` or another `X | Y` type now pauses cleanly, and the paused run is saved and resumes with `continue_run(run_id=...)`.
- **Mistral**: The `timeout`, `endpoint` and `safe_mode` parameters on `MistralChat`, and `endpoint` on `MistralEmbedder`, now work instead of raising a `TypeError`. `safe_mode` is deprecated in favor of `safe_prompt`.

## What's Changed
* [fix] Keep Chinese text readable in BaiduSearchTools output by @RaycarlLei in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11229
* fix: handle non-positive breakpoints and validate max_chunk_size in AgenticChunking by @Fazlul105 in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11231
* fix: run custom workflow steps function once when its body raises TypeError by @kausmeows in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11235
* fix: stop Postgres metrics refresh from loading the legacy runs column into memory by @sannya-singal in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11190
* feat: run Company automation hourly instead of every minute by @ysolanky in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11221
* fix: admit CORS-allowed browser origins on the MCP surface by @ysolanky in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11246
* feat: run a published MCP tool over HTTP by @sannya-singal in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/10666
* fix: serialize PEP 604 tool parameter types in UserInputField.to_dict by @ShaoLOWu in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11177
* refactor: rename Product-scoped Company tools by @ashpreetbedi in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11242
* fix: map Mistral client params onto the mistralai SDK and alias safe_mode to safe_prompt by @ysolanky in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno

title: crewAIInc/crewAI 1.15.29 — 1.15.29
body:
## What's Changed

### Features
- Add support for LiteLLM-compatible kwargs.
- Implement platform application search in CLI.
- Highlight action picker search in CLI.
- Trace conversation routes and public replies in flow.
- Select organization during login in CLI.
- Add offline jev routing and guardrail evaluation runner.
- Run integration app actions directly with call: tool.
- Promote AgentExecutor out of experimental status.
- Add Azure DocumentDB vector search integration.
- Add read-only notebook text loader and standard-library jsonl loader.
- Ensure crewAI eval keeps the evaluation's full data in the project.
- Enable crewAI eval to run the crew itself for verdict from one command.
- Allow crewAI eval to export evaluations as files.

### Bug Fixes
- Fix platform integration token derivation from login.
- Resolve logging issues by preserving JSON logs on serialization errors.
- Skip non-UTF-8 cached skill metadata.
- Fix tool actions to honor failure policies and get fresh usage budgets per kickoff.
- Prevent private memories without a source from leaking to every recall.
- Fix memory record retrieval order in LanceDBStorage.
- Restore task description when replanning fails.
- Stop agents from repeating the same tool call.
- Escape scope and id values in LanceDB filters.

### Documentation
- Update broken links in crewAI examples and observability guides.
- Fix dead links in tools documentation.

### Refactoring
- Refactor context compaction to be a BaseLLM capability.

### ⚠️ Compatibility Notes
* Remove shut-down Groq models `playai-tts`, `playai-tts-arabic`, `meta-llama/llama-guard-4-12b` and `meta-llama/llama-4-maverick-17b-128e-instruct` by @mekanbaymyradov in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/pull/10306

* Record what the user heard of ElevenLabs Agents replies they barged in on, adding the `OutputItemCut` lifecycle event by @DouweM in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/pull/10739
* Append the next hour to `LogfireMCP` history instead of rewriting its instructions, keeping the prompt cache by @DouweM in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/pull/10543

title: agno-agi/agno v3.1.7 — v3.1.7
body:
# Changelog

## Improvements:

- **OS Manager Tool Limits**: `OSManager` takes `tool_call_limit` (default `8`, per coordinator run, including delegations) and `member_tool_call_limit` (default `24`, per specialist invocation). Explanations stay scoped to the question and grounded in the Agno docs. Set either limit to `None` to restore unlimited tool use, as before. See [cookbook](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/main/cookbook/05_agent_os/29_manager/README.md).
- **Cartesia Default Model**: `CartesiaTools` now defaults to `sonic-3.6`. Cartesia sunsets the `sonic-2` snapshots, the previous default, on October 20, 2026.

## Bug Fixes:

- **Company Routines**: Editing a Product's `metadata` no longer unlinks its Routines. `SchedulerTools` and Studio can no longer delete, enable, disable or rewrite Company-managed schedules. OS Manager sends Routine and Product work to Product Manager. Under user isolation, Routines with no owner run again, and refresh archives only the caller's finished work.
- **Postgres Metrics**: `calculate_metrics()` works past the driver's query parameter limit (32,765 sessions on asyncpg, 65,533 on psycopg). On `AsyncPostgresDb`, a failed refresh now returns an error instead of a 200 with empty metrics.
- **v3 Migration on Postgres**: The sessions-to-runs migration streams rows through a server-side cursor. Memory is bounded by one batch, so large `sessions` tables no longer run out of memory.
- **Sandbox Checkpoints with Virtualenvs**: A workspace containing a Python virtualenv no longer fails checkpoint capture on its absolute interpreter links. A checkpoint that fails because of the workspace files now ends the run with a non-retryable error and releases the session, which previously stayed stuck in `finalizing`.
- **S3 Checkpoint Cancellation**: Cancelling `S3CheckpointStore.aopen_archive` no longer leaves the downloaded copy in scratch, and the cached-object digest check runs off the event loop.

## What's Changed
* fix: Move Cartesia's default TTS model to Sonic 3.6 by @jiangjiang248 in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/10750
* fix: stream the v3 sessions-to-runs migration on Postgres instead of loading it all into memory by @Himanshu040604 in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11183
* fix: checkpoint virtualenv links and release sessions whose files cannot be checkpointed by @ysolanky in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11191
* fix: bound OS Manager tool use and ground explanations by @ashpreetbedi in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11175
* fix: compute Postgres metrics past the driver query parameter limit by @sannya-singal in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11182
* fix: remove S3 checkpoint copies when an async open is cancelled by @ysolanky in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11194
* fix: keep Company Routines linked, routed and owned consistently by @ysolanky in https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/11184
* chore: Release v3.1.7 by @kausmeows in https://github.

title: agno-agi/agno v3.1.8 — v3.1.8
body:
# Changelog

## New Features

- Postgres Sandbox Checkpoint Store: Added `PostgresCheckpointStore` for storing sandbox checkpoints directly in PostgreSQL, allowing multi-replica deployments to restore sessions without S3 or shared filesystems. Checkpoints are chunked, written transactionally, deduplicated by SHA-256 and verified on read. It is opt-in; existing checkpoint defaults are unchanged. (#11186)
- Framework Managers as Routine Executors: Company Routines can now use the internal Product Manager or OS Manager as executors through declarations, the Routine API and human-chat configuration. Reserved manager IDs resolve only from the owning AgentOS and cannot be replaced by saved or user-defined components. Includes an optional weekly Product Manager review. (#11193)
- Sandbox Checkpoint Retention: Sandboxes now retain the three newest checkpoints per session by default. Configure `retain_checkpoints=None` to preserve every checkpoint. Unpublished or superseded checkpoints are retired and deleted after the run outcome is safely stored. (#11187)

## Improvements

- Sandbox Session Cleanup: Deleting a sandbox-backed session now removes its warm computer and associated checkpoint objects after the database transaction commits. Single, bulk and user-scoped session deletion are supported without affecting sessions the caller does not own. (#11187)
- OS Manager Specialist Visibility: Platform Builder and Platform Manager now appear as members of OS Manager in `/teams` and `/teams/os-manager-internal`. They remain excluded from the reusable application registry, top-level agent discovery and standalone agent routes. (#11198)
- Claude Defaults to Sonnet 5.5: `Claude()` now defaults to `claude-sonnet-5-5`, replacing the deprecated `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` before its retirement. Non-default `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k` values are dropped with a warning for newer Claude models that reject those sampling parameters. This behavior applies across Anthropic, Bedrock, Foundry and Vertex providers. (#11212)

## Behavior Changes

- Checkpoint Retention: Only the three newest sandbox checkpoints are retained by default. Opening a checkpoint for an older run can now raise `CheckpointObjectNotFound`. Set `retain_checkpoints=None` to restore the previous unlimited-retention behavior. (#11187)
- Durable Sandbox Startup Validation: AgentOS now fails at startup when a durable-queue sandbox uses the host-local default checkpoint store. Configure a checkpoint store shared by every replica, such as `PostgresCheckpointStore` or `S3CheckpointStore`. Previously this invalid configuration failed only on the first submission. (#11187)

## Bug Fixes

- Missing Sandbox Checkpoints: A committed checkpoint missing from storage now ends the turn with a clear, non-retryable error, retires the newly created computer and releases the session. Previously the run remained `RUNNING`, exhausted queue retries and blocked later turns on the session. (#11187)

# Changelog

## New Features:

- **Eval Case Run Arguments**: `Case` takes `session_id`, `user_id`, `session_state`, `dependencies`, `metadata` and `knowledge_filters`, forwarded to the agent or team run, and `input` accepts a `Message`, so a case can attach an image or file to the graded turn. Cases sharing a `session_id` run as consecutive turns. See [cookbook](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/main/cookbook/09_evals/suite/suite_session.py).

## Improvements:

- **OS Manager Docs Access**: OS Manager queries the Agno documentation directly for framework questions instead of delegating to Platform Manager, and keeps delegated tasks scoped to the question. `access_docs` now covers both.
 - **Result Offloading Search and Readback**: `search_result` returns separate passages from one long line, such as single-line JSON, instead of only the first match, and `read_result` takes `max_chars` to read a smaller excerpt.
 
## Bug Fixes:

- **ParallelTools**: Copying an agent or team with `ParallelTools`, as AgentOS does on every request, keeps the live SDK client and gives the copy its own settings, without `RLock` copy errors or `_state` finalizer warnings.

## [2.13.0](https://github.com/google/adk-python/compare/v2.12.0...v2.13.0) (2026-10-22)


### Highlights

This release stabilizes core features while introducing TypeSafe workflow classification, live audio interactions, MongoDB integrations, and execution performance improvements.

* **Stability**: Access 12 mature experimental features now promoted to stable status. See the [unit guide](https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/main/docs/guides/features/feature_registry/index.md) for more details. ([ea298d4](https://github.com/google/adk-python/commit/ea298d4bde4477daa6c419d45637f339eec86d58))
* **Classifiers**: Route workflows with TypeSafe's Jev models via the new `TypesafeClassifier` and `ClassifierNode`. Jev returns calibrated probabilities in a single forward pass, much faster than an LLM. See the [unit guide](https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/main/docs/guides/labs/classifiers/classifier_node/index.md) for more details. ([ddf8c55](https://github.com/google/adk-python/commit/ddf8c55eb6bc5e0c5fb90acbed3b66af939f7d7a), [e8c4bac](https://github.com/google/adk-python/commit/e8c4bacdfe675ceb5adcaf24ea005af94d271c68))

([2e7ef92](https://github.com/google/adk-python/commit/2e7ef926c953e5daab31cbc7ccb52fc77ebd9ae6))
* **MongoDB Sessions & Memory**: Persist sessions in MongoDB and share them across runner replicas with the new `MongoDbSessionService`. Add long-term memory without an embedding model using `MongoDbMemoryService`, which recalls past turns by keyword match on any MongoDB deployment, with no vector index needed. Both are experimental. See the [session service](https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/main/docs/guides/integrations/mongodb/session_service/index.md) and [memory service](https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/main/docs/guides/integrations/mongodb/memory_service/index.md) guides for more details. title: modelcontextprotocol/servers v2.1.0 — v2.1.0
body:
## Security fixes

v2.1.0 fixes eight vulnerabilities in three servers. Upgrade
`@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` and `@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything`
to 2.0.1, and `mcp-server-fetch` to 2026.10.24.

| Package | Affected | Fixed in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` | 1.0.0 through 2.0.0, and date versions through 2026.8.31 | 2.0.1 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything` | 1.0.0 through 2.0.0, and date versions 2025.9.24 through 2026.8.31 | 2.0.1 |
| `mcp-server-fetch` | through 2026.10.19 | 2026.10.24 |

### `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` 2.0.1

title: Tool-Calling LLM Agents Under Realistic MCP Faults: Scale Does Not Purchase Fault Tolerance
body: LLM agents increasingly rely on external tools exposed via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), yet current benchmarks assume tools respond correctly and on time, leaving agent resilience to realistic tool failures untested. We introduce MCP-Injector, a drop-in, protocol-aware fault-injection middleware that interposes on the MCP tool-call path with controlled persistence (permanent, transient, intermittent) and seedable schedules. Its fault model is calibrated to the observed incident distribution (failure mode x persistence) of the public MCP ecosystem, mined from 57,240 issue and pull-request threads across 1,774 open-source MCP repositories. In a 1,350-cell experiment crossing two backbone sizes (20B, 120B), three agent stacks (custom multi-round plan-and-execute, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain), and three fault injection conditions, we find that faults drawn from this permanent-heavy stress profile cause severe quality degradation (task-completion score falls by 60%, from 8.08 to 3.23 out of 10), and that scale does not purchase fault tolerance for the two gpt-oss backbones we test: the 120B retains no larger share of its fault-free score under faults (resilience-ratio model, $p = 0.96$), and its completion rate under faults is, if anything, lower (91.1% vs. 95.6%; difference 4.4 points, 95% CI $[-0.2, 9.3]$). Agent stacks differ in how well they absorb faults, which suggests that framework-level error handling matters more than model scale. These results demonstrate that capability benchmarks alone can mask operational brittleness, motivating protocol-aware fault injection as a complementary evaluation dimension for tool-calling agents.
author: Antonio Ken Iannillo, Joshua Segun Owotogbe, Roberto Natella, Francesco Avallone, Kristina Kudryavtseva

title: ReflectPO: Reflection-Guided Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
body: With external tools, large language models (LLMs) can tackle complex tasks through sustained environmental interaction. LLM-based agents are therefore increasingly used to tackle complex long-horizon tasks in real-world environments. However, these tasks involve sequential, interdependent decisions and changes in environmental states. Early execution errors affect subsequent interaction histories and environmental states, and their effects accumulate along the decision chain. To address this challenge, we propose Reflection-Guided Policy Optimization (ReflectPO), a reinforcement learning framework for autonomous error recovery in long-horizon tasks. ReflectPO comprises two core components. The first is Reflection-Guided Sampling. We use branch differences and repeated visits in interaction trajectories to construct hints for error recovery. The second is Tree-Structured Credit Assignment. We organize sampled trajectories into trees and assign action-level credit using parent--child reward differences and recovery gains. Experiments over two long-horizon tool-use benchmarks show that ReflectPO outperforms multiple existing baselines in most domains. It also achieves the best overall performance on average. Further analyses show that ReflectPO effectively improves agents' ability to recognize their own deviations, recover from erroneous states, and continue making progress toward task completion.
author: Rumei Li, Xunliang Cai

title: LongHaul-Bench: A Reproducible Benchmark for Long-Horizon Reliability of Self-Improving LLM Agents Under Industrial Edge Constraints
body: Self-improving agents built on large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for industrial fault diagnosis, but it is not known whether the experience such an agent accumulates over months of operation makes it more reliable or slowly corrupts it, least of all under edge-deployment constraints. We present LongHaul-Bench, a seed-reproducible synthetic industrial environment and protocol that follows an agent's knowledge state over about 1,000 sequential episodes with a quantized 3B-parameter model and a hard experience-memory budget. Across five independently generated worlds, experiential learning lifts exact accuracy over a frozen control by 3.8 points (complete rank separation; Holm-corrected p = .048). Plausibly corrupted feedback induces dose-dependent knowledge rot (-6.0 points at 40% corruption; -2.3, not significant, at 20%), whereas blatantly invalid feedback is inert. We explain these effects with a recall-precision decomposition computed on episode-matched pairs: memory adds about 9 points when a recall surfaces the correct precedent and removes about 20 points when it misleads, so memory helps only above a break-even recall precision of roughly 0.7. Plausible corruption leaves the cost of a misleading recall unchanged and instead lowers recall precision (0.81, 0.72, 0.65 at 0/20/40%); the precision drop alone accounts for the full loss at 20% and three-quarters of it at 40%. LLM-free manual-consistency gates recover the damage by restoring precision to 0.78, yet suppress two-thirds of memory's benefit when manuals are incomplete, and memory's value is an order of magnitude larger for a weaker 3B model family (+28 vs. +2.3 points). Generator, harness, run logs, and analysis scripts are released at https://github.com/vahit19/longhaul-bench.

title: Model Context Protocol and the Agent–Tool Ecosystem: A Systematic Survey of Standardizing AI Tool Integration
body: The usefulness of a large language model (LLM) agent is bounded by the tools it can reach. Until recently, every connection between an AI application and an external system—a database, a code repository, a SaaS API, a file system—was a bespoke, one-off integration, producing an N×M fragmentation problem: N applications times M tools, each pair wired by hand. The Model Context Protocol (MCP), introduced by Anthropic in November 2024, proposes to replace this patchwork with a single open standard, explicitly modeled on the Language Server Protocol's success in decoupling editors from language tooling. This paper presents a systematic survey of MCP and the agent–tool ecosystem forming around it. We describe the protocol's architecture—hosts, clients, and servers communicating over JSON-RPC—and its three server primitives (tools, resources, and prompts) together with client-side features such as sampling, roots, and elicitation. We analyze its transport designs (local stdio and remote Streamable HTTP), its evolving OAuth-based authorization model, and the security questions raised by third-party tool servers, including prompt injection through tool descriptions and over-privileged tool exposure. We survey adoption across IDEs, agent frameworks, and model providers; compare MCP with adjacent approaches—native function calling, OpenAPI-described tools, and agent-to-agent protocols such as A2A; and consolidate how tool-using agents are evaluated, from function-calling leaderboards to interactive agent benchmarks. We close with open problems: server trust and registry governance, the absence of a standard MCP-specific benchmark, versioning and capability drift, and the protocol's transition to neutral stewardship under the Agentic AI Foundation.

title: The Helpful Agent Problem: When Emergent Cooperation Among LLM Agents Bypasses Intended Workflows
body: LLM agents are increasingly deployed in collaborative settings where they pursue separate tasks while sharing resources and operating under review or oversight processes. Such settings create safety risks not only when agents are malicious, but also when they are simply trying to help. Prior work has largely studied adversarial or explicitly collusive behavior; we show that benign agents pursuing separate objectives can spontaneously cooperate in ways that bypass intended workflows. We call this the \emph{helpful agent problem}. We study long-horizon shared-resource environments in which agents sometimes depend on resources owned by their peers and cross-owner changes are normally mediated by a reviewer. When review becomes unavailable, agents begin making changes on one another's behalf despite having no shared reward or explicit incentive to cooperate. Crucially, these actions remain within each agent's local permissions while circumventing the system's intended oversight structure. We introduce \textsc{FavorBench}, a controlled benchmark with measurable downstream side effects, and adapt \textsc{CooperBench} to test the phenomenon in realistic repositories. Across two benchmarks and four models, we find that out-of-workflow favors emerge frequently. Further, in \textsc{FavorBench}, favors from at least three models cause significant harm to parties outside the interaction. These results reveal a distinct multi-agent safety challenge: cooperation itself can create pathways around system-level safeguards.
author: Moumita Choudhury, Amit Sarker, Shlomo Zilberstein
